messages:
Siobhán: Heads-up — I'm WFH in Dublin this week, anyone fancy a Temple Bar midday meetup on Thursday? 
Matt: yes please, free after 12:30. 
Leila: I can do 12:45, need somewhere with good veg options. 
Jordan: shout if we need a quieter spot (Temple Bar can be loud). 
Dara: for classic pub grub -> The Bank on College Green is solid. Burgers + fish and chips. :fries: 
Matt: The Bank is great but busy. For quieter, try 3FE — it's a cafe but decent sandwiches and walks to St Stephen's Green. 
Siobhán: any kid-friendly / highchair spots? Bringing my little one for daycare pickup after 2. 
Leila: Hatch & Sons do good kids meals and a relaxed vibe. 
Jordan: quick poll: do we want "classic pub" / "quiet cafe" / "something near Trinity" ? 
lunchbot: Poll created — Classic pub (2), Quiet cafe (1), Near Trinity (0) — vote with emoji. 
Matt: voted :beer: (classic pub) 
Leila: voted :coffee: (quiet cafe) — lean cafe9 if it's doable. 
Dara: :beer: — classic pub for the atmosphere, but open to Hatch if we need highchair. 
Siobhán: OK pub it is. Can someone check if Bank can seat 6 at 12:45? 
Jordan: I'll call them at 12:15 and post back. 
Leila: Also, for folks flying into Dublin later this month — if you want good cheap dinner after arrivals, try Foodtruck market on Dame Street (Wed nights). 
Matt: Re travel rec — if arriving early, grab an espresso at 3FE then walk to the Book of Kells to kill time. 
Jordan: Update: Bank said walk-ins only but big groups sometimes get space at the back, coming early helps. 
Siobhán: cool, I'll aim to be there 12:30 with stroller-friendly bag, ping me if plans change. 
Dara: tagging parking tip for visitors: Park Rite on Stephen's Court is cheapest short stay. 
Leila: cheers all — see you Thursday! :wave:
